name: receipt_lines
title: Receipt Lines
description: Expected against received against rejected, per ordered thing. This is the collection the discrepancy IS: three columns rather than one, because 'we received 8' is not an answer to 'the supplier billed us for 10'. quantity_expected is what the purchase order line said, stamped here so the sheet still reads correctly after somebody amends the PO; quantity_received is what went onto the shelf and is what composes the `purchase` stock move; quantity_rejected is what physically arrived and is going straight back. The gate that makes the fold trustworthy lives in hook_receipt_lines: cumulative quantity_received across every receipt of one order line may never exceed the quantity ordered, refused with all three numbers rather than a shrug, exactly as hook_shipment_lines does on the sales side. description is STAMPED from the order line at creation so a receiving sheet printed next year still says what the dock actually counted, even if the product has since been renamed (docs/logic-decisions.md #1).

fields.name: receipt_id
fields.label: Receipt
fields.help: Set once at creation and not intended to change after -- not schema read_only for the same reason order_lines.order_id is not: a required, client-submitted-at-creation field cannot also be read_only on this platform.

fields.name: order_line_id
fields.label: Order Line
fields.help: Which purchase order line these goods satisfy. Required, and not merely a cross-reference: without it the over-receiving gate has nothing to count against, and 'eight of something turned up' is not an answer to 'did the supplier send what we ordered?'. Plain text rather than a declared relation, so this package can be installed alongside an app-orders that is not there yet -- the same reasoning shipment_lines.order_line_id carries, and the hook does the real check and says so in words.

fields.name: product_id
fields.label: Product
fields.help: Optional cross-reference to app-catalog's products, mirroring order_lines.product_id. It is what the purchase stock move is composed against; a line with no product moves no stock, which is correct for a service, a delivery charge, or a free-text line that never sat on a shelf.

fields.name: description
fields.label: Description
fields.help: Stamped from the purchase order line at creation. The receiving sheet prints THIS, not a live product lookup: the paperwork about a delivery must keep saying what was counted off the pallet.

fields.name: quantity_expected
fields.label: Expected
fields.help: What the purchase order line said was coming, stamped at creation. Kept alongside the received count rather than looked up live, because a PO amended after the fact would otherwise rewrite history and make an honest short delivery look like a clean one. A count/measure, not money -- may be fractional, the same deliberate exception order_lines.quantity documents; read with Decimal everywhere.

fields.name: quantity_received
fields.label: Received
fields.help: What went onto the shelf. This is the number the `purchase` stock move is composed for and the number the PO's derived status is folded from; the over-receiving gate counts cumulative values of THIS field across every receipt against one order line. Zero is allowed and sometimes correct (the pallet arrived empty of this item), but a zero line must carry a rejected quantity or a discrepancy note -- see hook_receipt_lines.

fields.name: quantity_rejected
fields.label: Rejected
fields.help: Goods that PHYSICALLY ARRIVED and are being sent back -- damaged, wrong size, past date. They are NOT a short delivery, and conflating the two is how a supplier gets paid for what they never delivered: a short delivery means the goods were never sent and must never be invoiced, while a rejection means they were sent, we hold the evidence, and the argument is about credit. Rejected quantities compose NO stock move, because they never entered stock (system_receipt_posting).

fields.name: discrepancy_note
fields.label: Discrepancy Note
fields.help: Why the three numbers disagree, in the receiver's own words: 'two cartons crushed', 'supplier substituted the 500ml'. Free text on purpose -- a reason-code enum invented before anyone has read a hundred real ones is a taxonomy that makes the dock pick the closest wrong answer. Required by hook_receipt_lines on any line that received nothing, because a blank zero is indistinguishable from a data-entry slip.
